mainTopic: חגי's question to the כהנים, and which liquids of the מקדש are 'pure' (רב vs. לוי)
overview: This עמוד finishes an attempted proof from the question חגי הנביא asked the כהנים. The proof claims that wine and oil in the מקדש can become טמא. The גמרא rejects it, because it only works for רב, who already holds that altar liquids can become טמא. Next comes the full מחלוקת. רב says the כהנים erred, because the oil was a רביעי בקודש. שמואל says they were right, because the garment counts as an extra level, which makes the oil a חמישי. Each side is then challenged from the next פסוקים in חגי and defended. The גמרא then returns to יוסי בן יועזר's testimony. רב's version covers only the slaughterhouse liquids, while לוי's version covers all the altar liquids. The גמרא shows that לוי must agree with שמואל that the liquids can still become impure themselves, and that שמואל must accept רב's 'slaughterhouse' version. Finally, a ברייתא is quoted in support of each version, and the one for לוי is defended against a statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: רב says the priests made a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The proof from חגי's question ends with רב's statement that the כהנים answered wrongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: The priests erred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof it started on the previous עמוד. It quotes רב, who says the כהנים gave the wrong answer when they told חגי that the oil was טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, a chain of foods touch one another: bread, stew, wine, and then oil. The כהנים said the last item, the oil, stays טהור. If רב says they were wrong, then the wine and oil, which are liquids, really can become טמא. That is the point the proof is trying to establish.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the closing piece of a proof that started on the previous עמוד, based on the פסוק in חגי about bread, stew, wine, and oil.

phrases.english: And Rav said: The priests erred.
phrases.notes: So the oil really was impure, which means liquids can become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof from חגי's question, which began on the previous עמוד.
steps.raayaObject: That liquids of the מקדש (wine and oil) can become טמא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement that the כהנים erred when they declared the oil טהור.

steps.title: The proof only works for רב, who already agrees
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside. רב already holds that altar liquids become טמא, so his view proves nothing to someone who disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this reasoning work for anyone other than רב? רב teaches the testimony as 'the liquids of the slaughterhouse' are pure. But the liquids of the altar-house can become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. רב's statement only shows what רב himself thinks, and רב already agrees that wine and oil used on the altar can become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, two versions of the testimony were discussed. רב's version said only the slaughterhouse liquids (blood and water) are טהור, which leaves the altar liquids (wine and oil) able to become טמא. So the חגי story fits רב's own view, but it does not force anyone else to agree. Someone who reads the testimony as covering the altar liquids (לוי) can explain חגי's question another way: each item touched a ראשון directly, as Step 16 shows.

keyTerms.meaning: is this reasoning valid for anyone except...? (a formula that limits a proof to one opinion)
liquids of the slaughterhouse (blood and water)
liquids of the altar-house (wine and oil)

steps.confusionAlert: מַטְבְּחַיָּא (slaughterhouse) and מַדְבְּחַיָּא (altar) look and sound almost the same, but they mean different things. That small difference in wording is the whole key to this step.

phrases.english: Is this reasoning valid for anyone other than Rav?
Rav teaches the testimony as 'the liquids of the slaughterhouse' [are pure],
phrases.notes: Only the blood and water are covered by the leniency.

phrases.english: but the liquids of the altar-house do become impure.
phrases.notes: Wine and oil, like the ones in חגי's question, can become טמא according to רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only works within רב's own opinion. It cannot be used against the other view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof depends on רב, who already reads the testimony as limited to slaughterhouse liquids. Others can explain the חגי story differently.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא: a proof that relies on one אמורא's view cannot be used against someone who holds a different view.

steps.title: The disagreement itself: did the priests err?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes the original מחלוקת between רב and שמואל in full.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself: רב said the priests erred, and שמואל said the priests did not err.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב's statement was mentioned in passing, the גמרא now goes back and presents the whole disagreement. This step sets up the two explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only heard רב's side. Now we learn that שמואל disagrees and says the כהנים answered correctly. The next two steps explain the reason behind each side.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement quoted earlier in passing

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: This opens a full discussion of a statement quoted earlier.

phrases.english: Rav said: The priests erred,
and Shmuel said: The priests did not err.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the statement from step 1 and presents the full disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב says the כהנים erred. שמואל says they did not err.

steps.title: רב's reason: the oil was fourth-level impurity in sacred food
steps.stepSummary: According to רב, חגי asked about a רביעי בקודש. The כהנים said it was טהור, and that was a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said the priests erred: חגי asked them about a fourth level of impurity in sacred food, and they told him it was pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains why he thinks the כהנים made a mistake. In his reading, the oil was at the fourth level of טומאה, and in קודש even the fourth level is still טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב counts the chain like this: bread touches the שרץ and becomes ראשון. The stew becomes שני, the wine becomes שלישי, and the oil becomes רביעי. Since קודש is strict enough to become פסול even at the fourth level, the כהנים should have said the oil was טמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rests on a basic rule: קודש can become טמא at more levels than ordinary food. It reaches all the way to the fourth level.

phrases.english: Rav said: The priests erred —
he [חגי] asked them about a fourth-level [impurity] in sacred food,
phrases.notes: Chain: bread (1st), stew (2nd), wine (3rd), oil (4th).

phrases.english: and they told him it was pure.
phrases.notes: That answer was wrong, because a רביעי בקודש is פסול.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: אִישְׁתַּבֻּשׁ כָּהֲנֵי — רְבִיעִי בַּקֹּדֶשׁ בְּעָא מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב's side of the disagreement in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question was about a רביעי בקודש, which is טמא. So the כהנים' answer of טהור was a mistake.

steps.title: שמואל's reason: the oil was fifth-level, so pure is correct
steps.stepSummary: According to שמואל, חגי asked about a חמישי בקודש. The כהנים correctly said it was טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said the priests did not err: חגי asked them about a fifth level of impurity in sacred food, and they told him it was pure.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains why he thinks the כהנים were right. He counts one more step in the chain, which makes the oil a fifth level, and קודש does not become טמא at the fifth level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל counts the garment as its own level: the garment touches the שרץ and becomes ראשון. Then bread is שני, stew is שלישי, wine is רביעי, and oil is חמישי. Since טומאה in קודש stops after the fourth level, the oil really was טהור. So the two אמוראים agree on the rule and disagree only on how to count the chain.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל agree that קודש becomes טמא up to the fourth level, but not the fifth. They argue only about how to count the chain in חגי's question. רב says the oil was fourth, so the כהנים erred. שמואל says it was fifth, so they were correct.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב and שמואל argue about the rules of טומאה in קודש. They agree on the rules and only count the steps of the chain differently: does the garment count as its own level?

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: The priests did not err —
he asked them about a fifth-level [impurity] in sacred food,
phrases.notes: Chain: garment (1st), bread (2nd), stew (3rd), wine (4th), oil (5th).

phrases.english: and they told him: pure.
phrases.notes: This was correct, because קודש does not reach a fifth level.

steps.triggerLanguage: ושְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: לָא אִישְׁתַּבֻּשׁ כָּהֲנֵי — חֲמִישִׁי בַּקֹּדֶשׁ בְּעָא מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's explanation, set against רב's explanation in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question was about a חמישי בקודש, which is טהור. So the כהנים answered correctly.

steps.title: Where does שמואל get five levels from?
steps.stepSummary: The four foods in the פסוק fit רב's count of four levels. The גמרא asks how שמואל finds a fifth level.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רב: that is why the verse lists four things — bread, stew, wine, and oil. But for שמואל, where does he get five?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל. The פסוק lists only four foods, so how can שמואל say the question was about a fifth level?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב counts the four foods as four levels, so the oil is the רביעי. שמואל says the question was about a חמישי, but there are only four foods to count. He needs to find one more level somewhere in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (for one side). This sets up a challenge to the other side.
Bread, stew, wine, and oil — the four foods in חגי's question
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav,
that is why four are written:
bread, stew, wine, and oil.
phrases.notes: Four foods give four levels: the oil is the fourth.

phrases.english: But according to Shmuel,
where does he get five from?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב אַרְבְּעָה אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוּאֵל חַמְשָׁה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests שמואל's view from Step 5 against the wording of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that חגי asked about a חמישי בקודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names only four foods, which matches four levels. A fifth level seems to have no source.

steps.title: The garment itself is the first level
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the corner touched the food, not that the impure meat inside it did. So the garment is an extra level, which makes five.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'and his corner touched'? It is written 'and it touched with his corner' — meaning, with that which touched in his corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל from the exact wording of the פסוק. The food touched the garment, not the source of impurity, so the garment counts as a level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words בִּכְנָפוֹ mean the food touched the corner of the garment. The garment is the ראשון, the bread שני, the stew שלישי, the wine רביעי, and the oil would be the חמישי. This is the fifth level that שמואל needs.

keyTerms.meaning: And it touched with his corner — the exact words of the פסוק
Is it written...? A way of pointing out the exact wording of a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The food did not touch the impure meat directly. It touched the garment that held it. That is why the garment counts as its own level.

phrases.english: Is it written "and his corner touched"?
"And it touched with his corner" is written —
with that which touched in his corner.
phrases.notes: The garment that touched the impure item is itself a level of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי כְּתִיב וְנָגַע כְּנָפוֹ וְנָגַע בִּכְנָפוֹ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against שמואל in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the four foods are levels, so there can only be four.
steps.terutzMaskana: The garment is an extra level, so the oil is the חמישי.

steps.title: Challenge to רב from the case of a person who is טמא מת
steps.stepSummary: In the next פסוק the כהנים answered correctly about טומאת מת. For שמואל they never erred. For רב, why did they err in one case and not the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And חגי said: If one impure from a dead body touches any of these, does it become impure? And the priests answered and said: It becomes impure.' This makes sense for שמואל: since they did not err here, they also did not err there. But for רב, why did they err here, and why did they not err there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק, where the כהנים answered correctly about a person who is טמא מת. It uses this to challenge רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל there is no problem, because the כהנים were right in both questions. For רב, the כהנים were wrong about the שרץ case but right about the מת case. Why would the same כהנים make a mistake in one and not the other?

keyTerms.meaning: A person made impure by a dead body

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And Haggai said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יִגַּע טְמֵא נֶפֶשׁ בְּכׇל אֵלֶּה הֲיִטְמָא
phrases.english: If one impure from a dead body touches any of these, will it become impure?
And the priests answered and said: It will become impure."
phrases.notes: This answer is correct according to everyone.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Shmuel,
since here (the שרץ case) they did not err,
there (the מת case) they also did not err.
But according to Rav,
why is it different here, that they erred,
and why is it different there, that they did not err?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע וַיֹּאמֶר חַגַּי אִם יִגַּע טְמֵא נֶפֶשׁ בְּכׇל אֵלֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending שמואל, the גמרא now challenges רב from the next פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the כהנים erred in the שרץ case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same כהנים answered the מת case correctly. It is strange to say they were expert in one case and mistaken in the other.

steps.title: The כהנים knew טומאת מת well but not טומאת שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, answers for רב: the כהנים were experts in the laws of a dead body but not in the laws of a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: They were experts in the impurity of a dead body, but they were not experts in the impurity of a creeping animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רב. The כהנים knew one area of הלכה well and another area poorly, so they could be right in one case and wrong in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two answers are not inconsistent. Each one reflects how much the כהנים knew about that type of טומאה. With this answer, רב's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity from a dead creeping animal

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the כהנים erred only about the שרץ, because they did not know those laws well. According to שמואל, they never erred. The garment counts as an extra level, which makes the oil the חמישי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
They were experts in the impurity of a dead body,
but they were not experts in the impurity of a creeping animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ בְּקִיאִין הֵן בְּטוּמְאַת מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two cases differ in how much the כהנים knew
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the כהנים erred in one case, they should have erred in the other as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their knowledge was strong in טומאת מת and weak in טומאת שרץ, so the two answers are not inconsistent.

steps.title: רבינא's different answer: the dead-body case was only a third level
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers for רב in a different way. In the שרץ case the question was about a רביעי, but in the dead-body case it was only about a שלישי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: There it was a fourth level; here it was a third level.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives another answer to the question from Step 8: according to רב, why did the כהנים err in one case and not the other? He says the two questions were not equally hard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the dead-body case, the count starts from the corpse itself, which is the strongest source of טומאה, so the last food only reaches the level of שלישי. In the שרץ case, the last food reached רביעי בקודש, which is a subtler law. The כהנים knew the easier law and slipped on the harder one, so they could have known both topics equally well.

keyTerms.meaning: there (the first case, about the שרץ)
here (the second case, about the dead body)

steps.confusionAlert: Both of חגי's questions use the same chain of four foods. Yet the levels come out different, because the dead-body chain starts from a stronger source (the corpse is אבי אבות הטומאה). So the same last food is only a שלישי in that case.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
There (the שרץ case) it was a fourth level,
phrases.notes: A harder law: a רביעי is impure only for holy food.

phrases.english: here (the dead-body case) it was a third level.
phrases.notes: An easier, better-known law, which they got right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the same קשיא that רב נחמן answered in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the two questions were at different levels of difficulty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two questions were equally hard, so getting only one right makes no sense for רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dead-body question was only about a שלישי (easy). The שרץ question was about a רביעי בקודש (hard), so erring only there makes sense.

steps.title: The verse calls their offerings impure, which is a problem for שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The next verse says the offerings are טמא. That fits רב, since the כהנים erred, but it seems to contradict שמואל, since for him they never erred.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And Haggai answered and said: So is this people, and so is this nation before Me, says God,' etc. Granted according to רב, that is why it is written 'impure.' But according to שמואל, why 'impure'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings חגי's response to the כהנים' answers, which ends with the word 'טמא'. It uses this word to challenge שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the כהנים did not know the laws of טומאה well. So it makes sense that the נביא says their offerings were impure. For שמואל, they answered everything correctly, so why would the verse accuse them of offering in טומאה?

keyTerms.meaning: granted, it makes sense (for one view)
but (for the other view, there is a problem)

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted verse ends with 'וגו׳' (etc.). The word 'טמא' that the גמרא focuses on comes later in the verse: 'ואשר יקריבו שם טמא הוא', meaning 'and what they offer there is impure.'

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And Haggai answered and said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּן הָעָם הַזֶּה וְכֵן הַגּוֹי הַזֶּה
phrases.english: So is this people and so is this nation
before Me, says God,' etc.
phrases.notes: The verse goes on: 'and what they offer there is impure.'

phrases.english: Granted according to Rav,
that is why it is written 'impure.'
phrases.notes: They erred in the laws of טומאה, so their offerings were impure.

phrases.english: But according to Shmuel,
why 'impure'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רב to challenging שמואל from the next verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that the כהנים answered correctly (Step 5).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נביא calls their offerings טמא, which suggests they were not careful about טומאה. That contradicts the claim that they knew the law.

steps.title: The verse is a surprised question, not a statement
steps.stepSummary: For שמואל, the word 'טמא' is read as a surprised question: 'Is it really impure?'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is expressing surprise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל. The נביא is not declaring their offerings impure. He is asking in surprise, 'Could their offerings really be impure?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: By reading the verse with a question tone, it stops being an accusation. Read this way, the verse actually supports the idea that the כהנים knew the laws of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: he is expressing surprise (a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: He is expressing surprise.
phrases.notes: Read as: 'And what they offer there is impure?!' Surely not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא against שמואל in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the verse: a statement becomes a rhetorical question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse declares their offerings impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse asks in surprise whether they could be impure, which implies they were not.

steps.title: But 'all the work of their hands' sounds like a statement
steps.stepSummary: The verse also says 'וכן כל מעשה ידיהם', and that sounds like a flat statement of blame, not a question.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written, 'And so is all the work of their hands'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 12. The same verse clearly criticizes the people, so it is hard to read it as a surprised question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'And so is all the work of their hands' compares the כהנים to the whole people and condemns them all. That reads like a real accusation, which weakens the 'surprised question' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is written! (introduces a challenge from a verse)

phrases.english: But it is written, 'And so is all the work of their hands'!
phrases.notes: This sounds like a direct statement of blame.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the verse as a surprised question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The surrounding words are clearly a condemnation, so the verse is not asking. It is accusing.

steps.title: Their other sins are counted as if they offered in impurity
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא (or רב אשי) explains that because the people sinned in general, the verse describes them as if they had offered sacrifices in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, and some say רב אשי, said: Since they corrupted their deeds, the verse considers them as if they offered sacrifices in impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final answer for שמואל. The verse really is blaming them, but not for an actual mistake about טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'טמא' in the verse is a description of their spiritual state, caused by their general wrongdoing. It is not a report that their sacrifices were actually ritually impure. So שמואל can still say the כהנים knew the laws of טומאה and answered correctly.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse treats them as if

steps.whatToRemember: For שמואל, the כהנים in חגי's time knew the laws of טומאה. The verse's word 'טמא' is about their sins in general, not a real ritual mistake.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said,
and some say it was Rav Ashi:
Since they corrupted their deeds,
the verse considers them
as if they offered sacrifices in impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 and closes the challenge against שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the verse: the blame is figurative and comes from their general sins.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'טמא' means they actually offered sacrifices in ritual impurity, which would show they did not know the law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse condemns them for other sins and describes them as if they offered in טומאה. Their knowledge of the laws is not questioned.

steps.title: Back to יוסי בן יועזר: slaughterhouse liquids or altar liquids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to יוסי בן יועזר's testimony that the liquids of the מקדש are pure. רב's version says 'liquids of the slaughterhouse', and לוי's version says 'liquids of the altar'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: רב teaches 'liquids of the slaughterhouse,' and לוי teaches 'liquids of the altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: With 'גופא', the גמרא leaves the חגי discussion and goes back to a statement quoted earlier, to discuss it directly. It sets out two versions of the wording, which prepares for the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's wording, 'בית מטבחיא' (the slaughterhouse), covers only the liquids found where animals are slaughtered: blood and water. לוי's wording, 'בי מדבחיא' (the altar), is broader. It also includes the wine of נסכים and the oil of מנחות. So this is a real disagreement about how far the purity rule reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter itself (going back to analyze a statement mentioned earlier)
liquids of the slaughterhouse (blood and water)
liquids of the altar (also wine and oil)

steps.confusionAlert: The two words look and sound almost the same: מַטְבְּחַיָּא is the slaughterhouse and מַדְבְּחַיָּא is the altar. Only one letter changes, but the scope of the law changes a lot.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute decides which liquids in the מקדש are exempt from becoming impure. That shapes the rest of the סוגיא about משקי בית מטבחיא.

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself:
phrases.notes: Back to יוסי בן יועזר's testimony quoted earlier.

phrases.english: Rav teaches 'liquids of the slaughterhouse,'
phrases.notes: Blood and water.

phrases.english: and Levi teaches 'liquids of the altar.'
phrases.notes: Also includes wine of נסכים and oil of מנחות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the חגי discussion and returns to the earlier statement of יוסי בן יועזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב reads the testimony as 'liquids of the slaughterhouse' (blood and water). לוי reads it as 'liquids of the altar' (also wine and oil).

steps.title: לוי's view works if he agrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: If לוי holds like שמואל that the liquids can become impure themselves, then חגי's question can be explained as each item touching a ראשון directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: For לוי, it works well if he holds like שמואל, who said the liquids are 'pure' only in that they do not make other things impure, but they themselves can become impure. Then you can explain the case as one where all the items touched a first-degree impure object.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins testing whether לוי's version fits חגי's question. This is a setup line: it shows the option that works before raising the option that does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For לוי, altar liquids like wine and oil do not pass impurity to other things, so חגי's case cannot be a chain where one item touches the next. The only way the items become impure is if each one touched a ראשון directly. That needs the liquids to be able to become impure themselves, which is exactly שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well / it is fine (used to set up 'but if...')

phrases.aramaic: לְלֵוִי, הָנִיחָא אִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כִּשְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: According to Levi, it works well if he holds like Shmuel,
who said: 'pure' means they do not make others impure,
phrases.notes: שמואל's reading of יוסי בן יועזר's testimony

phrases.english: but they can become impure themselves
— you can find the case where all of them touched a first-degree impure object.
phrases.notes: Each item touched the ראשון directly, not one after another in a chain

steps.triggerLanguage: לְלֵוִי, הָנִיחָא אִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes לוי's version from step 15 and checks how it fits חגי's question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי's version fits חגי's question if the liquids can become impure themselves, as שמואל says

steps.title: If לוי agrees with רב, the case cannot be found
steps.stepSummary: If לוי held like רב that the liquids are completely pure, wine and oil could never become impure, and חגי's case would be impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he holds like רב, who said the liquids are truly pure, how could you ever find this case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the other option: לוי agreeing with רב. It shows that this option makes חגי's question impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the liquids are fully pure. They cannot pass impurity to others, and they cannot become impure themselves. Then wine and oil could never become impure in any way, so חגי's question about whether they are impure would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find (such a case)?

phrases.english: But if he holds like Rav,
who said: 'pure' means actually pure,
— how can you find the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The 'but if' half of the הניחא/אלא pattern begun in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that לוי agrees with רב on the meaning of 'דכן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If altar liquids cannot pass impurity on (לוי) and cannot become impure at all (רב), then wine and oil can never be impure, and חגי's question has no case.

steps.title: לוי must agree with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that לוי has to hold like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are forced to say that he holds like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the לוי half of the analysis. Only one option works, so לוי must agree with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two options were tested. Holding like רב left no possible case, so לוי must hold like שמואל: the liquids do not make others impure, but they can become impure themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Perforce / you are forced to say

phrases.english: Perforce, he holds like Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the forced conclusion from steps 16 and 17
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: לוי (altar liquids) must agree with שמואל (the liquids can become impure themselves but do not make others impure)

steps.title: שמואל's view works if he agrees with רב's version
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל holds like רב's version (only slaughterhouse liquids), then altar liquids like wine and oil do make others impure, and חגי's chain case works.
steps.simpleTranslation: For שמואל, it works well if he holds like רב, who taught 'liquids of the slaughterhouse'. Then the altar liquids do make other things impure. So it is only a רביעי that does not make a חמישי, but a שלישי does make a רביעי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now runs the same test for שמואל. This is again a setup line: it shows the option that works before raising the one that does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the כהנים answered correctly. The chain went up to a רביעי, and a רביעי does not create a חמישי. For that chain to exist, wine and oil must be able to pass impurity along, at least from שלישי to רביעי. That only works if the decree covered just the slaughterhouse liquids, as in רב's version.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquids of the slaughterhouse (water and blood)
Liquids of the altar (such as wine and oil)
Fifth-degree impurity (does not exist even for holy items)

steps.confusionAlert: Here רב is cited for his VERSION of the testimony ('slaughterhouse'), not for his view that 'דכן' means fully pure. These are two separate disputes. That is why שמואל can disagree with רב on one and agree with him on the other.

phrases.aramaic: וְלִשְׁמוּאֵל, הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב,
phrases.english: And for Shmuel, it works well if he holds like Rav,
who taught: 'liquids of the slaughterhouse'
but as for the liquids of the altar
— they make other things impure too,
it is only a fourth-degree item that does not make a fifth,
but a third-degree item does make a fourth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִשְׁמוּאֵל, הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same test from steps 16–18 to שמואל, in the other dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל's reading of חגי (the chain stops at רביעי) fits if altar liquids do pass impurity, as in רב's version

steps.title: If שמואל agrees with לוי's version, the fourth-degree detail makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: If altar liquids never pass impurity (לוי's version), there is no reason to single out a רביעי not making a חמישי, since even a שני or שלישי would not make others impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he holds like לוי, who taught 'liquids of the altar', why speak specifically of a רביעי not making a חמישי? Even a שני and a שלישי would not make others impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the other option for שמואל, agreeing with לוי's version, and shows it does not fit the details of חגי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to לוי's version, wine and oil cannot pass impurity to anything. Then the reason the last item stays pure would have nothing to do with being a רביעי. Already at the second and third steps, nothing would pass on, so the focus on רביעי would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? (why single this case out?)

phrases.english: But if he holds like Levi,
who taught: 'liquids of the altar',

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִירְיָא רְבִיעִי דְּלָא עָבֵיד חֲמִישִׁי?
phrases.english: why single out a fourth-degree item not making a fifth?

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ שֵׁנִי וּשְׁלִישִׁי נָמֵי לָא עָבְדִי!
phrases.english: Even second and third would not be made either!
phrases.notes: Since altar liquids pass on no impurity at all according to לוי

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The 'but if' half of the הניחא/אלא pattern begun in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that שמואל agrees with לוי's version (altar liquids)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If altar liquids pass on no impurity at all, the chain would stop at the very first step, so emphasizing that a רביעי cannot make a חמישי would be meaningless.

steps.title: שמואל must agree with רב's version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שמואל has to hold like רב's version of the testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are forced to say that he holds like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the שמואל half of the analysis. Only one option fits, so שמואל must accept רב's version ('slaughterhouse liquids').
steps.deeperAnalysis: Agreeing with לוי's version left the focus on רביעי unexplained. So שמואל must hold that the decree covered only slaughterhouse liquids, and altar liquids like wine and oil still pass impurity along.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two separate disputes. (1) What does 'דכן' mean? רב: fully pure. שמואל: they only do not make others impure. (2) Which liquids are covered? רב: slaughterhouse liquids. לוי: altar liquids. The conclusion is that לוי must agree with שמואל on dispute 1, and שמואל must agree with רב on dispute 2.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that each אמורא's reading of the חגי verses forces a matching position in the other dispute. This turns two separate arguments into one connected system.

phrases.english: Perforce, he holds like Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the forced conclusion from steps 19 and 20
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל must accept רב's version: only slaughterhouse liquids were declared pure, and altar liquids still pass impurity along

steps.title: Each version has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that there is a ברייתא supporting רב and a ברייתא supporting לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that fits רב's version, and a ברייתא was taught that fits לוי's version.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is telling us that both versions of the testimony have backing in a ברייתא, and it will quote each one next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already saw two versions: רב (only the slaughterhouse liquids, blood and water) and לוי (all altar liquids, including wine and oil). This line does not prove anything yet. It previews that neither version is invented, because each matches a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him / supporting his view
A teaching of the תנאים left outside the משנה

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav,
it was taught in accordance with Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּלֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling which version each אמורא holds, the גמרא now looks for תנאית support for both versions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רב's version and לוי's version are supported by a ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא that supports לוי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists blood, wine, oil and water as 'altar liquids'. If they became impure inside the מקדש they stay pure even when taken out. If they became impure outside and were brought in, they are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in line with לוי: blood, wine, oil and water are 'liquids of the altar'. If they became impure inside the מקדש and someone took them outside, they are pure. If they became impure outside and someone brought them inside, they are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that backs לוי's version. It includes wine and oil in the pure 'altar liquids'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's version only covers blood and water from the slaughterhouse. This ברייתא adds wine and oil and calls them משקי בי מדבחיא, which is exactly לוי's wording. It also gives a rule about where the liquid became impure. Impurity that happened inside does not take hold in a way that passes on, so the liquid stays pure even after it leaves. Impurity from outside stays even after the liquid enters.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquids of the altar (wine, oil, water, blood)
Pure (here: they do not pass on impurity)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'pure' depends on where the liquid is now. In this ברייתא, what counts is where it BECAME impure: inside means pure even after leaving, outside means impure even after entering.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Levi:
The blood, the wine, the oil, and the water,
liquids of the altar,
that became impure inside and one took them outside —
phrases.notes: The impurity happened inside the מקדש.

phrases.english: they are pure.
If they became impure outside and one brought them inside —
they are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This fills in the first half of the preview from Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: לוי's version, that all altar liquids (including wine and oil) are pure
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists wine and oil together with blood and water as משקי בי מדבחיא

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי says 'only in their place'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. רבי יהושע בן לוי said altar liquids are pure only 'in their place', which seems to mean that once they are taken out they lose the purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't רבי יהושע בן לוי say: 'About altar liquids, they only said they are pure in their place.' Doesn't that come to exclude liquids that became impure inside and were taken outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first half of the ברייתא, the part that says liquids made impure inside stay pure even when taken out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In their place' sounds like the purity only works while the liquid sits inside the מקדש. If so, liquid that became impure inside and was carried out should become impure, which contradicts the ברייתא. The phrase 'מאי לאו' shows the גמרא is suggesting this reading, not stating it as certain.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
Liquids of the altar —
they did not say 'pure' except in their place.
Is it not —
to exclude those that became impure inside and were taken outside!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the first rule of the ברייתא quoted in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that liquids made impure inside and taken outside are pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Only in their place' suggests the purity ends once the liquid leaves the מקדש, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: 'In their place' excludes a different case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע בן לוי meant to exclude liquids that became impure outside and were brought inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It comes to exclude liquids that became impure outside and were brought inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing which case רבי יהושע בן לוי was excluding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי was not talking about liquid taken out of the מקדש. He was excluding liquid that became impure outside and was then brought in. That matches the second half of the ברייתא, so there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: No,
it is to exclude those that became impure outside and were brought inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge from Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which case the statement excludes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע בן לוי excluded liquid made impure inside and taken out.
steps.terutzMaskana: He excluded liquid made impure outside and brought in, which agrees with the ברייתא.

steps.title: But he said 'in their place'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the words 'in their place' sound like the liquid must still be inside now.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'in their place'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from the wording. 'In their place' seems to mean the liquid must stay inside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid that became impure outside and was brought in is already inside now. So if 'in their place' means 'where it is now', that liquid should count as pure. That would make the answer in Step 25 fail.

phrases.english: But he says "in their place"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the answer given in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that 'in their place' excludes liquid brought in from outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain words point to the liquid's current location, not to where it became impure.

steps.title: 'In their place' means where they became impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יהושע בן לוי meant: they are pure only if they became impure in their place, inside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: they only said 'pure' about liquids that became impure in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the wording of רבי יהושע בן לוי. 'In their place' describes where the liquid became impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in their place' go with 'became impure', not with where the liquid is now. So liquid made impure inside stays pure even after it leaves, and liquid made impure outside stays impure. This fits the ברייתא exactly, so the support for לוי stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The purity of altar liquids depends on where they BECAME impure (inside the מקדש), not on where they are now. The ברייתא of לוי survives the challenge.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
They did not say 'pure' —
except for those that became impure in their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the wording challenge from Step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In their place' means where the liquid is located now.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In their place' means where the liquid became impure.

steps.title: The ברייתא that supports רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that blood and water, the slaughterhouse liquids, are pure if they became impure, whether in vessels or on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in line with רב: blood and water, the liquids of the slaughterhouse, that became impure, whether in vessels or on the ground, are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second ברייתא promised in Step 22, the one that backs רב's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא names only blood and water and calls them משקי בית מטבחיא, which is רב's wording. Wine and oil are not included. It adds that the purity applies whether the liquid is in a vessel or on the floor.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquids of the slaughterhouse (blood and water)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ברייתא: only blood and water (slaughterhouse). לוי's ברייתא: blood, water, wine and oil (altar). Each version has its own source.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מַטְבְּחַיָּא (slaughterhouse, רב) with מַדְבְּחַיָּא (altar, לוי). The two words differ by one letter but mean different groups of liquids.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav:
The blood and the water,
liquids of the slaughterhouse,
that became impure, whether in vessels or on the ground —
are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about רבי יהושע בן לוי, the גמרא returns to the second half of the preview from Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב's version, that only the slaughterhouse liquids (blood and water) are pure
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that names only blood and water as משקי בית מטבחיא
